mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An upward crossing of the unemployment rate above 3.5% triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days due to heightened market uncertainty.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite UNRATE crossing above 3.5% in the specified window, or returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in federal funds rates and growth in demand (measured by GDPC1) over 1 month leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced borrowing costs and expanded investment opportunities.
failure_condition: The interaction of FEDFUNDS down and GDPC1 up occurs but 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or remain below baseline levels.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in federal funds rates predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate sustained economic growth and lower financing costs.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, 20-day forward returns do not rise significantly above baseline (p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over 3 months predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as increased production capacity signals economic strength and investor confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to rise significantly above baseline (p > 0.05) despite a sustained upward trend in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: An abrupt increase in employment numbers (PAYEMS) exceeding 152,383 in a month triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days due to concerns about over-employment and potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain positive despite PAYEMS crossing above 152,383 in the specified window, or returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both consumer demand (GDPC1) and housing demand (HOUST) over 1 month lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as expanded economic activity boosts market optimism.
failure_condition: The simultaneous rise in GDPC1 and HOUST does not result in significantly positive 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05) or returns remain below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 4.0%), a decline in federal funds rates predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as policy easing becomes more critical to stabilize the labor market and stimulate growth.
failure_condition: In high-unemployment regimes, 20-day forward returns do not rise significantly above baseline (p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS declines.
